heard: A 1,000-foot city killer slipped right past Earth without anyone noticing. On March 31, 1989, astronomers Henry Holt and Norman Thomas spotted a faint streak at Palomar Observatory. When they calculated its orbit, the data revealed something terrifying. Nine days earlier, in late March 1989, this massive rock had swept past our planet. Designated 4581 as Cleps, it missed us by 425,000 miles, roughly twice the distance to the moon. Had it struck an ocean, calculations showed it would unleash the power of a 600-megaton atomic explosion. The shock of missing this close called forced governments to establish modern planetary defense networks. It was a chilling reminder of how easily a massive asteroid can sneak past us.
